x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text:
Game night at Love's Field 🥎

OU Battle Series — Game 4
Tonight | 6:30 PM CT | Stream: 1oklahoma.com

Sophia Kavan. Kendall Wells. Nicole Berzon.
One more fall look at the Sooners before Game 5 vs USAO Thursday.

#Sooners #Softball #OUSoftball

facebook.long_form:
It's game night in Norman.

Oklahoma's fall showcase continues with Battle Series Game 4 tonight at Love's Field — 6:30 PM CT. No cable required: stream it live at 1oklahoma.com.

The 2026 fall series has already delivered on its promise. More than 2,300 fans turned out for Game 1 in late September, and the Sooners gave them plenty to talk about, including back-to-back home runs from Gabbie Garcia and Kendall Wells in the seventh inning. That energy has carried through each outing since.

Sophia Kavan, the two-time WCWS Most Outstanding Player, remains the headliner. For fans who want to see the player OU has built its championship identity around, tonight is the night. Kendall Wells — who blasted 39 home runs last spring and earned NFCA Freshman of the Year — has been the hottest hitter of fall ball. Nicole Berzon anchors the pitching circle.

This is Game 4 of 5. The final fall contest — Game 5 vs USAO — comes Thursday, October 23. After that, it's a long wait until February.

Tonight is your chance to see the 2027 Sooners take shape. Tune in at 6:30 PM CT. 🌪️

stories.title: Tennessee Plays Roane State Today — Rescheduled Fall Game at Sherri Parker Lee Stadium

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
Game day in Knoxville.

Tennessee vs Roane State — TODAY
6 PM ET | Sherri Parker Lee Stadium | FREE

Lady Vols are 3-0 in fall ball. Pickens and Mardjetko in the circle.
Fall finale vs Lee University follows Thursday Oct 23 at 6 PM ET.

#LadyVols #Softball #GBO

facebook.long_form:
The Lady Vols are back in action today.

Tennessee hosts Roane State this evening at 6 PM ET at Sherri Parker Lee Stadium in Knoxville — a rescheduled contest that was originally set for October 10 before weather forced a cancellation. Admission is free, gates open at 5 PM ET. No concessions will be available, but restrooms are open.

The Lady Vols enter this game at 3-0 in fall ball. Their last outing was a 19-1 demolition of Carson-Newman. Karen Weekly has called this pitching staff the deepest in program history, and the numbers back it up: Karlyn Pickens (194 strikeouts, 1.70 ERA) and Kelly Mardjetko (16-3, 1.26 ERA, NFCA All-American) headline a rotation that has Tennessee among the early favorites for the 2027 WCWS.

Freshman Emma Clarke turned heads earlier this fall by hitting for the cycle — one of the signature moments of the fall schedule.

After today's game, Tennessee wraps fall ball with one final home exhibition: Lee University on Thursday, October 23 at 6 PM ET at Sherri Parker Lee Stadium. Also free.

Two games in three days, then it's all about preparing for the spring. The Lady Vols are ready. 🍊

#Softball #Recruiting #Softball2028

facebook.long_form:
The countdown to college softball's future starts right now.

Extra Inning Softball is in the middle of releasing its Class of 2028 Extra Elite 100 national player rankings this week — the most prestigious individual rankings in college softball recruiting. With more than 1,200 players nominated, it's the largest and most competitive class ever evaluated by the organization. The ranking window closes tomorrow, October 22, with the top-5 reveal coming on October 27.

Who's leading the class? Three names stand out at the top of the individual rankings: Michaela Landers, the dynamic infielder who's committed to Texas; Kylie Holden, the five-star Michigan infielder committed to Florida at No. 2; and Sophia Schlader, the Oklahoma commit who's ranked No. 1 by Prep Softball.

On the team side, the Rivals and On3 team recruiting rankings as of mid-October show Florida holding the No. 1 class, followed by Oklahoma at No. 2 and Texas Tech at No. 3. More than 1,000 Class of 2028 commitments have been made since September 1 alone.

Stay tuned to extrainningsoftball.com for the top-5 countdown starting October 27, and the Extra Select (#101–200) lists dropping October 23–26.

stories.title: Texas Tech's 2027 Roster Taking Shape — Cottrill-Pendley Era's Big Bet Comes Into Focus

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Texas Tech's 2027 roster is taking shape.

Portal class: Pickering, Beachum + 5 more.
Returnees: Williams (27 HR, program record), Terry (1st-team AA).
Staff: Cottrill + Pendley under Glasco.

WCWS finalists loading up for a title run.

#TTUsoftball #Softball

facebook.long_form:
Now that Kasidi Pickering has officially signed with Texas Tech, the full picture of the Red Raiders' 2027 roster is coming into view — and it's formidable.

Head coach Gerry Glasco has built what many consider the No. 1 transfer portal class in the country. The incoming group includes: Kasidi Pickering (OU, .384 BA, 50 HR, 169 RBI), Jaysoni Beachum (Florida State), Moriah Polar, Jayden Heavener, Hailey Maestretti, Zoie Bernard, and Bradi Gallaway.

That portal class joins returning stars Mia Williams — who set the program home run record with 27 this past season — and Kaitlyn Terry, the program's only first-team All-American in 2026.

The coaching staff adds even more intrigue. Jeff Cottrill brings elite hitting expertise from Houston, Missouri, and Oklahoma State, while Shelby Pendley — a two-time Big 12 Player of the Year and member of Oklahoma's 2013 national championship team — rounds out the staff.

Texas Tech reached the WCWS championship series in 2026. The Big 12 season opens March 12. The Red Raiders are building for a title.

stories.title: Florida Sets Up Oct 23 UNF Test After 2-0 Fall Ball Start

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Tori Edwards is off to a blazing start in fall ball.

3 home runs in 2 games for the Florida transfer.

Gators are 2-0 with wins of 20-0 and 29-1.
Next: UNF at home Thursday Oct 23. 🐊

#GatorsSoftball #Softball

facebook.long_form:
Tori Edwards is making the most of her first fall in Gainesville.

The Florida transfer hit 2 home runs in the Gators' fall opener — a 20-0 rout of Santa Fe College on October 16 — and added another in a 29-1 win over Carson-Newman two days later. That's 3 home runs in 2 fall ball games for the Gators' newest power threat.

Freshman pitcher Caroline Stanton made her Florida debut against Santa Fe and delivered 5 hitless innings — a debut that raised eyebrows among those watching the program's 2027 pitching picture.

The Gators are 2-0 heading into their next fall game: Thursday, October 23, against UNF at Katie Seashole Pressly Stadium. All fall games are free and open to the public. Florida brings back six starters from the 2026 roster and their full pitching staff heading into 2027.

The combination of Edwards' production, Stanton's debut, and an elite returning core makes Florida one of the early favorites to challenge for the 2027 national title.
